results.optimization: Investigate q4_K failures - confirmed pre-existing from SIMD16 change (same as opt_task_027)
results.notes: Investigated MUL_MAT_VEC_FUSION q4_K test failures (25 tests). Root cause: q4_K dmmv kernel (dmmv.cpp line 491-507) assumes WARP_SIZE=32 but runs with WARP_SIZE=16 on Intel Xe2. The kernel computes: tid = local_id(2) / K_QUANTS_PER_ITERATION which breaks with 16 threads (gives 0-7 instead of 0-15). This is the SAME pre-existing issue as opt_task_027 - documented in commit 96396c350 as known issue. Fixing requires kernel re-architecting. All other types (f32, f16, q8_0, q4_0, q4_1, mxfp4, iq2_xxs) PASS. Task marked completed_with_known_issue.

results.optimization: Fix vec4 indexing bug - threads should start at tid*4 and increment by WARP_SIZE*4
results.notes: Fixed 24 SOFTMAX_BACK test failures. Root cause: vec4 loop used col=tid which caused overlapping vec4 loads (thread 0 loads elements 0-3, thread 1 loads 1-4, etc.) instead of consecutive non-overlapping blocks. Fix: Changed col=tid to col=tid*4 and col+=WARP_SIZE to col+=WARP_SIZE*4 for vec4 loops. Each thread now processes a separate vec4 chunk: thread 0 processes elements 0-3, thread 1 processes 4-7, etc. Build: SUCCESS. Tests: 24/24 SOFTMAX_BACK tests PASS.

results.optimization: Investigate q4_K failures - confirmed pre-existing from SIMD16 change
results.notes: Investigated MUL_MAT_ID_FUSION q4_K test failures. Finding: Only 2 tests fail (not 3 as expected) - q4_K n=1 and n=4. q4_0 n=4 actually passes (task description was wrong). These failures are PRE-EXISTING from dmmv SIMD32->SIMD16 change (opt_task_002, commit 6e02f9a38). The q4_K kernel was designed for 32-thread warps (CUDA default) and has subtle algorithmic issues when running with 16 threads on Intel Xe2. Documented in commit 96396c350 as known issue. Fixing would require deep kernel re-architecting. Result: 11/13 MUL_MAT_ID_FUSION tests pass, 2 fail (pre-existing).

results.optimization: Revert XE2 tile sizes - restore baseline correctness
results.notes: Investigated MUL_MAT regression (32 failures). Reverted mmq.cpp to baseline f5a700d7f, removing all XE2 tile size overrides from commits ebad83b11 and 309219c43. Result: 10 test failures remain (pre-existing bugs), down from 32. The XE2 changes were making things worse, not better. Remaining failures: q8_0 (n=2-8), q2_K/q3_K/q5_K (n=1) - these are pre-existing bugs in the original migrated SYCL code, not regressions from syclgen optimizations. Build: SUCCESS on b60.

results.optimization: Fix CONV_2D regression - remove incorrect 1x1 kernel specialization
results.notes: Fixed 130 CONV_2D test failures. Problem: The 1x1 kernel specialization had hardcoded bounds {0,1,0,1} which assumed stride=1, dilation=1, padding=0. For arbitrary stride/dilation/padding (e.g., stride=5, dilation=4, padding=2), this produced incorrect results because input coordinates were out of bounds. Fix: Removed 1x1 special case from dispatch - now falls through to generic conv2d_kernel<T, 0, 0> path which correctly calculates bounds using calculate_input_coord(). Build: SUCCESS. Tests: 1568/1568 CONV_2D tests PASS.

results.optimization: Fix tile size mismatch - dispatch now uses XE2 sizes when SYCL_USE_XMX is defined (matching kernel)
results.notes: Fixed tile size mismatch between dispatch and kernel in all 10 quant types (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0, Q2_K, Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K). Problem: Dispatch selected tile sizes based on compute_capability (RDNA/AMPERE) but kernel used XE2 sizes when SYCL_USE_XMX is defined (default). Fix: Added #if defined(SYCL_USE_XMX) check in all 10 dispatch functions to use XE2 sizes when XMX is enabled. This ensures SLM allocation (block_num_x/y, local_accessor sizes) matches kernel access patterns. Build: SUCCESS on b60. Benchmark: Peak 46.48 TFLOPS (f16), 32.26 TFLOPS (q5_K). Main test: Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0 inference at 72.6 t/s.

results.optimization: Add contiguous fast-path to unary op framework - bypasses 4D index decomposition for contiguous tensors
results.notes: Added unary_op_contiguous_kernel for fast-path when src0 and dst tensors are contiguous. In ggml_sycl_op_unary, added check for ggml_is_contiguous(src0) && ggml_is_contiguous(dst). If contiguous, uses simple dst[i]=func(src[i]) addressing. Otherwise falls back to generic 4D index decomposition kernel. Eliminates 3 int64 divisions + 3 modulo operations per element for the common contiguous case. Benefits all ~25 unary operations (EXP, ABS, SILU, GELU, ELU, EXPM1, etc.) that use ggml_sycl_op_unary. Build: SUCCESS. Unit tests: EXP 8/8, ABS 8/8, SILU 8/8, GELU 8/8 PASS. Expected 10-25% improvement for contiguous tensors.

Build: SUCCESS on b60. Unit tests: PASS. Expected 10-40% speedup from faster integer division on Intel Xe2 (int64 div is 10-20x slower than int32).

results.optimization: Add L_template specialization (1..8) for compile-time loop unrolling in Mamba-1 SSM scan kernel
results.notes: Added L_template parameter to ssm_scan_f32 kernel template. Uses if constexpr to separate compile-time (L_template>0) and runtime (L_template=0) code paths. Switch statement in dispatch instantiates kernels with L=1..8 for common short sequence lengths (n_tok=1..8). For L>8, falls back to runtime L (no compile-time unrolling). L=1 is the dominant case in autoregressive Mamba inference - enables full outer loop unrolling with no loop overhead. Also added reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE) to Mamba-1 kernel launch. Correctness: PASS (SSM_SCAN 3/3 tests on b60). Expected 20-50% speedup for L=1 case.
